claims.text: The alloy has the nominal composition Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The starting alloy is additively manufactured.
The starting alloy has an fcc matrix.
Degradation during elevated-temperature gas exposure is governed jointly by elemental composition, processing, and microstructure.
The interaction of composition, processing, and microstructure influences protective oxide-layer formation.
The interaction of composition, processing, and microstructure influences the underlying microstructural evolution during exposure.
Protective oxide-layer formation and microstructural evolution mediate degradation.
The proposed exposure domain is 500-1000 °C for 1-100 hours in air or inert gas.
Elevated-temperature exposure will produce degradation, microstructural changes, and mechanical-property evolution relative to the as-fabricated baseline.
The alloy is expected to maintain its strength and fatigue performance during the proposed exposures.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes exposure to reducing gases, but the stated gas conditions include only air and inert gas; an inert gas is not a reducing-gas condition.

The predicted outcome merely states that mechanical properties will evolve, without predicting retention of strength or fatigue performance, while the falsification rule treats failure to retain those properties as contradictory to the hypothesis.
